answer_short.case-1: Chinese graphite goes in, and graphite goes out to seven US battery and car makers. Who owns the plant isn't in the registry.
answer_short.case-2: BTR's 100% ownership is on record. The first graphite left BTR's own Indonesian plant for Tangier in Aug 2026, and nothing has been exported yet.
answer_short.case-3: The Oman plant isn't in the data yet. Zhongke graphite reaches the US today through Malaysian cell plants.
answer_short.case-4: Korean-owned, with Chinese graphite inputs. It sells to the same US buyers as BTR Indonesia.
answer_short.case-5: No Chinese-owned anode maker is shipping to the US from five corridors. Putailai's Malaysian plant is still being built.
answer_short.case-6: Chinese anode graphite goes in and finished cells go out to US buyers, from a plant owned by China's EVE Energy.
answer_short.case-7: Gotion's Chinese plants ship cells, packs and graphite to its US sites, which its annual report says it wholly owns, though no US record shows it.
answer_short.case-8: A non-Chinese chain from Mozambique to Louisiana, but the same mine also supplies Chinese-owned plants.
answer_short.case-11: CATL's 100% ownership is on record, but EU-internal trade is invisible: only Chinese factory equipment shows up, and no battery materials.
answer_short.case-10: CATL's group owned Linergy until June 2026, when Japan's TDK bought it. Sayari still shows the old Chinese chain.
answer_short.case-9: Yes, but not via Morocco yet: BTR graphite reached Ford's Michigan plant from Indonesia in 2026, and BlueOval SK from China in 2025.
answer_short.case-12: Huayou's Indonesian nickel plant sends its output to Chinese refiners and traders. No nickel goes directly to the US, and the hop to US cathodes isn't joined by any record.

case-1.title: Natural graphite from African mines
case-1.text: Natural graphite reaches the plant from Syrah's mine in Mozambique and from ERG Madagascar.

case-1.title: Chinese graphite and petroleum coke
case-1.text: BTR and a trader in the BTR Building ship artificial graphite and petroleum coke to the plant.

case-1.title: BTR's plant in Indonesia
case-1.text: The plant processes these inputs into battery anode material.

case-1.title: Out to US battery and car makers
case-1.text: Artificial graphite ships to Ultium Cells, SK Battery America, StarPlus Energy, GM, Tesla, HSBMA and Ford's Marshall plant.

case-1.title: Who owns the plant
case-1.text: BTR's own filings give it a 60% stake. No registry record in Sayari shows this.

case-2.title: Who owns the plant
case-2.text: BTR owns the plant 100%, through holding companies in Singapore.

case-2.title: First graphite shipped
case-2.text: BTR's own Indonesian plant shipped the first graphite, 1,240 t, in Aug 2026.

case-2.title: BTR's plant in Tangier
case-2.text: The plant is still under construction.

case-2.title: No exports yet
case-2.text: Nothing has been exported, so the route stops here for now.

case-3.title: Who owns the plant
case-3.text: Zhongke Electric's group holds the Omani plant through a Hong Kong company.

case-3.title: The planned plant in Sohar
case-3.text: The plant is still being built, and no shipments from it appear in the records.

case-3.title: Today's route: graphite to Malaysia
case-3.text: Zhongke graphite already reaches cell plants in Malaysia run by EVE Energy and Linergy Power.

case-3.title: Then on to the US inside cells
case-3.text: Those plants ship to US buyers, including Briggs & Stratton and Eaton.

case-4.title: Natural graphite from Mozambique
case-4.text: One shipment from Syrah's mine in Mozambique reached POSCO Future M.

case-4.title: Graphite inputs from Qingdao
case-4.text: Qingdao companies shipped natural graphite and carbon inputs to the plant.

case-4.title: POSCO Future M in South Korea
case-4.text: The plants process these inputs into battery anode material.

case-4.title: Out to the same US buyers as BTR
case-4.text: Anode material ships to GM, SK Battery America, Tesla, Panasonic and XALT.

case-4.title: Who owns the plant
case-4.text: POSCO Holdings holds 58.2%. None of the 50 ownership paths checked leads to a Chinese owner.

case-5.title: Who owns the plant
case-5.text: Putailai owns the plant 100%, through a Singapore company.

case-5.title: Zichen's plant in Kedah
case-5.text: The plant is still under construction.

case-5.title: No exports yet
case-5.text: No shipments from this plant appear in the records, so the route stops here for now.

case-6.title: Anode graphite arrives
case-6.text: Zhongke, BTR, Shanshan and Qingdao Taidongrui ship anode graphite to the plant, including from BTR's Indonesian plant.

case-6.title: EVE's cell plant in Kedah
case-6.text: The plant makes finished battery cells, so the graphite is now inside a product.

case-6.title: Finished cells to US buyers
case-6.text: Cells ship to Briggs & Stratton, Milwaukee Tool, Stanley Black & Decker, Energizer and others. US customs records list them as cells, not graphite.

case-6.title: Who owns the plant
case-6.text: EVE Energy owns the plant through EVE Asia in Hong Kong.

case-7.title: Direct from Gotion's Chinese plants
case-7.text: Gotion's Chinese plants ship cells, packs and graphite straight to its US sites.

case-7.title: Gotion's sites inside the US
case-7.text: No third country is involved: these sites are in California and Illinois.

case-7.title: Who owns the sites
case-7.text: Gotion's annual report says it wholly owns them, but no US record shows it.

case-7.title: Onward sales are unclear
case-7.text: The only onward links are leads, so the route stops here.

case-8.title: Natural graphite from Mozambique
case-8.text: Syrah's Balama mine ships natural graphite to Syrah's own plant in Louisiana.

case-8.title: One shipment from China
case-8.text: One shipment of artificial graphite came from Qingdao Mien New Material.

case-8.title: Syrah's plant in Vidalia
case-8.text: The plant processes natural graphite into anode material.

case-8.title: Out to Tesla
case-8.text: Tesla is the US buyer linked to the plant.

case-8.title: The same mine also sells elsewhere
case-8.text: The same mine ships to BTR Indonesia and to Chinese buyers, so one mine can feed both kinds of chain.

case-8.title: Who owns the chain
case-8.text: Australia's Syrah Resources owns both the mine and the plant.

case-9.title: BTR Indonesia to Ford's Michigan plant
case-9.text: BTR Indonesia graphite reached Ford's Marshall plant in 2026, about 1,160 t. Seven of the 11 rows were loaded in China.

case-9.title: BTR's sales arm to BlueOval SK
case-9.text: BTR's Shenzhen sales arm and BTR Jiangsu shipped to BlueOval SK, Ford's venture with SK, in 2025.

case-9.title: Ford's battery plants
case-9.text: Ford's plants are the end of this route. BlueOval SK's sites are in Kentucky and Tennessee.

case-9.title: The Tangier contract
case-9.text: A China Baoan filing says Ford agreed to prepay US$120m to BTR's Tangier company. It is one filing, Ford hasn't confirmed it, and Tangier has shipped nothing yet.

case-10.title: Graphite and materials from China
case-10.text: Zhongke Shinzoom and Shanshan ship graphite, and Xiamen Ampace ships other cell materials.

case-10.title: Cells to US buyers
case-10.text: Cells ship to Eaton, Milwaukee Tool, Stanley Black & Decker and Techtronic.

case-10.title: Owner until June 2026
case-10.text: CATL's group owned the plant through Ampace.

case-10.title: Owner since June 2026
case-10.text: Japan's TDK bought the plant through its Singapore company. On 5 Nov 2026, Sayari still showed the old Chinese owners.

case-11.title: Who owns the plant
case-11.text: CATL owns the plant 100%, through CATL (Hong Kong).

case-11.title: Factory equipment only
case-11.text: Chinese production equipment appears in the records. No battery materials do.

case-11.title: CATL's plant in Debrecen
case-11.text: The plant is still under construction.

case-11.title: The route goes dark
case-11.text: Trade between EU countries leaves no customs record, so the route stops here.

case-12.title: Huayue's nickel plant
case-12.text: Huayou's plant in Indonesia produces a nickel intermediate.

case-12.title: Who owns the plant
case-12.text: Company filings put Huayou's stake at 57%.

case-12.title: Out to Chinese refiners
case-12.text: The nickel intermediate ships to Huayou companies, CMOC and other Chinese buyers. None ships directly to the US.

case-12.title: Huayou precursor to South Korea
case-12.text: Huayou companies shipped cathode precursor to POSCO Future M.
case-12.gap: No record joins this step to the one before it.

case-12.title: POSCO to US buyers
case-12.text: POSCO Future M shipped to StarPlus Energy and GM.
case-12.gap: No record joins this step to the one before it.

case-1.plant: PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Material

chain.name: BTR New Material Group Co., Ltd.
chain.stake: 60% (BTR exchange filings; not in Sayari). The other 40% is held by Stellar Investment (Singapore)

chain.name: PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Material

case-1.visibility: Not in Sayari's registry data. BTR's own exchange filings state 60%; the 40% holder, Stellar Investment Pte. Ltd., is owned by Ever Rising Ltd and linked to Tsingshan by a single press report (unverified).
case-1.inputs: Chinese artificial graphite (HS 3801) from BTR and a trader in the BTR Building; natural graphite from Mozambique, Madagascar and the UAE.
case-1.us_exposure: Ultium Cells (Warren, Spring Hill), SK Battery America, StarPlus Energy, General Motors, Tesla

open_questions.q: Who ultimately owns the 40% holder, Stellar Investment Pte. Ltd., and its parent Ever Rising Ltd? A single press report links it to Tsingshan (unverified).
open_questions.doc: Singapore ACRA business profile for Stellar Investment Pte. Ltd. (shareholders and officers), then the registry filing for Ever Rising Ltd in its home jurisdiction.

open_questions.q: Does BTR control the board and key decisions, which matters for the PFE effective-control test?
open_questions.doc: The PT's deed of establishment and latest amendments (akta), held by Indonesia's AHU registry, and the BTR–Stellar joint-venture agreement.

case-2.status: Under construction; first graphite received Aug 2026

chain.name: BTR New Material Group Co., Ltd.

case-2.visibility: Visible in registry data. The BNUO-owned company is 100% BTR at every step. The anode company (BTR Mediterranean Anode) is owned through Rian International Holding (Singapore), whose shareholder is a Singapore record of BTR.
case-2.inputs: Construction goods from China, then 1,240 t of artificial graphite from BTR's Indonesian plant (19 Aug 2026).
case-2.us_exposure: None yet. Ford has been reported as an expected customer.

open_questions.q: Is BTR Mediterranean Anode (the Rian-owned company) the anode plant, and is it 100% BTR?
open_questions.doc: BTR's own announcement on the Beijing Stock Exchange (stock 835185), and Singapore ACRA profiles for Rian International Holding.

open_questions.q: Who owns Rian International Holding, parent of the second Moroccan BTR company?
open_questions.doc: Singapore ACRA business profile for Rian International Holding Pte. Ltd.

open_questions.q: Which Moroccan company will run the anode line?
open_questions.doc: Morocco's trade-register extract (OMPIC / RC Tanger) for both companies, or a BTR announcement on the Beijing Stock Exchange.

case-3.plant: Zhongke Xingcheng Sohar New Material Technology
case-3.status: Under construction (ground broken 8 May 2026; first building topped out 10 Sep 2026, company post)
case-3.visibility: Registry visible inside China; the Hong Kong and Oman steps rest on the company's filing.
case-3.inputs: None yet. Zhongke's Chinese plants already supply Malaysian cell makers.
case-3.us_exposure: Indirect today, through cells made in Malaysia (see Case 6).

open_questions.q: Who are the registered shareholders of the Sohar project company?

open_questions.q: Is Zhongke Shinzoom (HK) Holdings 100% held by Zhongke Star City?

case-4.visibility: Visible in registry data; no Chinese owner among 50 ownership paths.
case-4.inputs: Chinese natural and spherical graphite from Qingdao suppliers (to Dec 2023 in the data). Korea imports all its spherical graphite from China until POSCO's Saemangeum plant starts in late 2027.
case-4.us_exposure: General Motors, SK Battery America, Tesla, Panasonic Energy, XALT; Ultium Cells by contract

open_questions.q: What share of POSCO Future M's anode is made from Chinese-origin graphite, and who owns its Chinese graphite suppliers?
open_questions.doc: A supplier origin certification from POSCO Future M, plus China's national enterprise credit system (NECIPS) records for the Qingdao suppliers.

case-5.visibility: Visible in registry data; two Shanghai-based directors, one named Han Zhongwei.
case-5.us_exposure: None yet from this plant. The group's Chinese anode company, Jiangxi Zichen, sent 10 rows to US buyers in 2024–25.

open_questions.q: Do the two Malaysian directors also act for Putailai in China, which bears on effective control?
open_questions.doc: Malaysia SSM company profile (directors' ID numbers) compared with Putailai's annual-report list of directors and senior managers.

case-6.visibility: Visible in registry data; the same directors (Liu Jincheng, Chan Tsun Ming) sit on both the Hong Kong and Malaysian boards.
case-6.inputs: Anode graphite from Zhongke Shinzoom, BTR, Shanshan and Qingdao Taidongrui; 91% of all inbound rows left from China.
case-6.us_exposure: EVE Energy North America, Briggs & Stratton, TTI, Milwaukee Tool, Stanley Black & Decker, Energizer and others

open_questions.q: After the June 2026 sale to TDK, does Linergy still buy anode material from CATL-group or Chinese suppliers?
open_questions.doc: Updated SSM shareholder filing for Linergy Power, and TDK's supplier disclosures or a direct supplier certification.

open_questions.q: What does EVE's 1260H listing mean for buyers of EVE Malaysia cells?
open_questions.doc: The Federal Register notice (Doc. 2026-11571) and the buyer's own legal advice. The listing restricts US defense procurement, not commercial purchases.

case-7.plant: Gotion, Inc. (Fremont, CA) and Gotion Illinois (Manteno, IL)

chain.name: Gotion High-Tech Co., Ltd.
chain.stake: Volkswagen (China) 24.28%; would fall to 18.98% when a pending sale completes

case-7.visibility: Visible from the Chinese side: registry data plus the parent's annual report, which names both US companies as wholly owned. No US record lists shareholders.

case-7.us_exposure: Gotion's own US entities; storage customers such as Richardson Electronics (announced partner)

open_questions.q: Is there any US record of who owns Gotion, Inc. and Gotion Illinois?
open_questions.doc: Gotion's FEOC/PFE certification to customers, or ownership disclosures in Illinois or Michigan state incentive filings. California's Statement of Information lists officers, not shareholders.

case-8.status: Commercial ramp-up since Sep 2026; first sales targeted Dec 2026 quarter
case-8.visibility: Partly visible in registry data; the percentages come from Syrah's own annual report.
case-8.inputs: Natural graphite from Syrah's Balama mine (Mozambique, 95% owned); some processing equipment and one small graphite lot from China.
case-8.us_exposure: Tesla and Lucid offtake agreements (final qualification pending)

open_questions.q: Is Twigg Exploration & Mining 95% owned by Syrah, as the annual report says?
open_questions.doc: Mozambique's Boletim da República company publication, or the Maputo commercial registry (CREL) extract.

case-11.status: Modules since autumn 2024; trial cell production since 22 Sep 2026; no series-production date announced
case-11.visibility: Visible in Hungarian registry data (100% CATL Hong Kong) and in China's outbound-investment directory.
case-11.inputs: Only Chinese production equipment is visible (7 rows from Yantian, Aug–Dec 2025). Battery materials from inside the EU leave no customs record.
case-11.us_exposure: None visible. The plant supplies European carmakers.

open_questions.q: What share of CATL (Hong Kong) does CATL hold?
open_questions.doc: CATL's annual report subsidiary list (SZSE 300750), or the Hong Kong Companies Registry annual return.

open_questions.q: Where do the plant's cathode and anode materials come from?
open_questions.doc: Supplier due-diligence reports under the EU Battery Regulation (from Aug 2027), or a direct supplier declaration; customs data can't see EU-internal trade.

case-10.status: Operating; sold to TDK in June 2026
case-10.owner_top: TDK (Japan) since Jun 2026; before that CATL group (59.5% via Xiamen Ampace)
case-10.visibility: Sayari still shows the old chain (Ampace HK → Xiamen Ampace → CATL 59.5%). The sale to TDK appears only in TDK's filings.
case-10.inputs: 2,679 of 2,759 inbound rows from China: graphite (Zhongke Shinzoom, Shanshan), cathode powder (XTC, Pulead, B&M), electrolyte (Tinci, Capchem), foil.
case-10.us_exposure: Eaton (after the sale), Milwaukee Tool, Stanley Black & Decker, Techtronic and Ampace's Hong Kong company (before the sale)

open_questions.q: Exact date the sale completed, and whether the Malaysian registry shows TDK's company as shareholder.
open_questions.doc: Malaysia SSM company profile (shareholder register) for Linergy Power, or TDK's completion notice.

open_questions.q: Did Xiamen Ampace own 100% of Ampace (Hong Kong)?
open_questions.doc: Hong Kong Companies Registry annual return (NAR1) for Ampace Technology Limited.
